Parole Boards

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Convicted child rapist Bob Hewitt has been released on parole despite objections by his victims. Should paedophiles be granted parole?

Unique Selling Point:
Interviews with Olivia and Amanda, two of Hewitt's victims.
Interview with parole Review Board Chair, Judge Siraj Desai
Interviews with attorneys of Hewitt and attorney of his victims


Summary:
In 2015 former Wimbledon doubles champion Bob Hewitt was convicted of the rape and indecent assault of three former girls that he coached. He was sentenced to 8 years imprisonment, but because of his advanced age he was ordered to serve only 6 years. In 2019 Bob Hewitt was granted parole, but because DCS had not informed his victims, nor given the opportunity to object, this was overturned. Parole Review Board Chair Siraj Desai ordered that his parole be cancelled. He was to participate in Victim/Offender Dialogue and undergo psychotherapy.
The victims declined to participate in the VOD process.
In February 2020 Hewitt's lawyers brought an urgent application to force DCS to consider Hewitt for parole. They succeeded and the Parole Board convened on 24th March at St Alban's Prison in PE, in contravention of the Disaster Management Act which states that no visits to any correctional services centres are allowed.

Further information:
Olivia Jasriel's attorney, Tania Koen informed DCS that her client would be accompanied by Luke Lamprecht (WAMAC) and her partner. When they arrived at the prison they were told that DCS had never received the email and the Parole Board Chair refused to allow them to attend. Olivia was supported by her attorney only.
All reports which were read out in support of Hewitt's release stated that he has a grandiose sense of self, does not take responsibility for his actions and shows no remorse. In person, in front of the parole board, Hewitt told Olivia he had done nothing wrong and that she was a liar.
Despite not meeting the criteria for parole, the Board decided to release him.

We will delve into who serves on parole boards? Whose interests are they meant to serve? Which parole boards have vacancies? Can paedophiles be rehabilitated? Should paedophiles and child rapists be placed on parole? Couldl Bob Hewitt re-offend, even though he is now 80-years old?

Extra Budget Items:
In the absence of any travel, would it be possible to hire a cameraman in Cape Town to film the interview with Judge Desai, and in PE to film the interviews with The two attorneys and the Parole Board Chairperson?

Script:


PAROLE BOARD


V/O: In 2019 South Africa saw widespread protests against gender-based violence. Young and old took to the streets saying enough is enough.

Crowd: “Enough is enough!”

V/O: President Ramaphosa addressed thousands of protesters gathered outside Parliament, promising stricter punishment.

Cyril: “The men who violate women, who rape women and who kill women must stay in jail for life.”

V/O: But convicted women and child rapists continue to be released on parole.

Link: Just last month we saw the release of another child rapist – perhaps South Africa’s most famous paedophile – Bob Hewitt. It took his victims over 30 years to finally get justice and put him behind bars. It took the St Alban’s Parole Board just a few hours to release him and send him home.
Sfx: “In the Men’s Doubles South Africa is represented by Bob Hewitt and Frew McMillan.”
V/O: Grand slam champion Bob Hewitt was a household name in South African tennis, who also coached young players. But in 2015 he was convicted of raping two former students. Sue-Ellen Sheeyen was 12-years-old at the time, and Twiggy Tolken was just thirteen. He was also convicted of indecently assaulting another teenager whose identity is protected by the court. Judge Bert Bam took Hewitt’s age into account, and sentenced the 75 year-old to an effective 6 years in jail. The convicted paedophile appealed his sentence, but this was dismissed by both the Supreme Court of Appeal and the Constitutional Court.
Olivia: We had gotten justice. What nobody told us was that six years would not be six years. Nobody told us it would effectively be three years.
V/O: Sue-Ellen has since changed her name to Olivia Jasriel. She and the other two victims were shocked to discover that the St Alban’s Parole Board had convened without their knowledge, and granted Hewitt parole in August last year.
Olivia: I felt very minimized; I felt what did we do this for? My constitutional rights were just completely disregarded.
V/O: Prisoners are entitled to be considered for parole once they’ve served half their sentence – except in the case of a life sentence. But victims are equally entitled to object, in person or in writing. However, there’s a gaping flaw in this process.
Link: Prison authorities are supposed to notify victims when offenders are going to a parole hearing to give them the opportunity to object. But that can only happen if they know who you are. They don’t come looking for you. The onus is on you, the victim, to find out where the offender is being held and then give the prison your contact details.
V/O: Despite having the victims details, Correctional Services failed to notify them of Hewitt’s hearing. In a response to Carte Blanche, the Department says they and the parole board took into account Olivia's earlier representations, when Hewitt applied to convert his sentence to correctional supervision. But Justice Minister Ronald Lamola intervened and Hewitt’s parole was later cancelled. Advocate Johann Engelbrecht is Hewitt’s legal representative.
Masa: How did you and Bob Hewitt feel when the Parole Review Board cancelled his parole?
Johann: He was disappointed; anybody would be disappointed. You are released on parole and a person comes from outside - it was only the Minister – cancels your parole release.
Masa: Why do you, Mr Hewitt and his wife believe he deserves the right to freedom?
Johann: Anybody has the right to freedom.
Masa: But he was convicted of rape?
Johann: Ja, I appreciate that, but in my opinion he was not guilty and should not have been sentenced.
V/O: Judge Siraj Desai is the Chairman for the National Council of Correctional Services and heads up the Parole Review Board.

They can review the decisions made by individual parole boards around the country. He reviewed the Hewitt matter.

Siraj: All we said was you cannot release this offender without victim offender dialogue taking place. I set aside the decision of the parole board and sent it back to them to reconsider the matter together with inputs from the victims.
V/O: Tania Koen represents two of Hewitt’s victims, and noted another crucial recommendation.
Tania: The department must pursue individual psychotherapy for the offender so that he could gain insight into his offences.
Masa: Johann Engelbrecht yesterday told us that Hewitt attended two therapy sessions. For any sex offender is two sessions enough?
Tania: I cannot possibly think that two sessions could be enough, but that’s my lay person’s opinion.
V/O: Luke Lumprecht represents Women and Men Against Child Abuse, and has vast experience in helping victims to navigate the criminal justice system.

Luke: As a child rights, child protection community we believe that our voices should also be heard in parole hearings because parole makes provision that the community’s needs and wishes are taken into consideration when parole is granted, and particularly because we are specialists in that field.
V/O: He’s been involved in this case from the beginning - and along with Tania - accompanied Olivia to the parole board hearing in March this year. But the Parole Board would not allow him to address the hearing.
Link: Most of us have never been to a parole board meeting, and because the proceedings are confidential we are not allowed to film one. But they are held inside the prison, in an ordinary boardroom, where the victims have to sit at the same table as their perpetrator.
Olivia: They put us in a room directly opposite each other. It just takes you straight back to when I was 12.
V/O: Correctional Services presented the findings of Hewitt’s case management committee.
Olivia: And there was a document probably of about three or four hundred pages of all the psychometric testing, psychological testing that he’s done. Every single report that they read came back that he is not rehabilitated; he lives in denial; he shows remorse and he takes no accountability for what he has done to us. At the end of the day it would have been nice to have had “I’m sorry for what I did to you”.
Johann: He said he is not guilty so he’s not going to ask for forgiveness.
Masa: So how’s he been rehabilitated if he feels he’s done nothing wrong?
Johann: He didn’t do anything wrong, and he went through every class that was presented to him in prison and they prison found him to be a suitable candidate because will not commit another crime again.
V/O: But according to international paedophile expert Dr James Cantor, a paedophile cannot be reformed.
James: We can’t rehabilitate a paedophile in the sense that there’s no known way to convert a paedophile into a non-paedophile. There’s a cross-wiring in the paedophiles. They are correctly perceiving a child to be a child, but it seems to be evoking the sexual and the flirtatious responses, rather than the parental and avuncular responses.
Masa: Is paedophilia a sexual preference?
James: Yes it is. It’s a basic, innate, neurological inborn sexual attraction pattern and it cannot change.
V/O: Dr Cantor has studied the brains of over 250 paedophiles through MRI scans.
James: Paedophilia – the sexual attraction pattern to children – is a brain phenomenon. These people’s brain structures are significantly different from people who are not paedophilic. Whatever chain of events it is that led to these brain differences, the first links of that chain go back to birth.
V/O: Despite objections from all 3 victims, Hewitt was released on parole on the 24th of April.
Masa: Do you think the parole board hearing took your clients’ objections seriously?
Tania: Definitely, no comment.
Olivia: When I went into that hearing a decision had already been made. So they’ve insulted my intelligence and insulted my integrity, and they wasted my time and my money.
Siraj: Whatever the offence, the man reaches the age of 80, we are not in a position to second-guess the court that sentenced him to 6 years in prison. There are no indications that he would re-offend at the age of 80, then one is just being vindictive in refusing parole.
V/O: And the Department told Carte Blanche that on parole Hewitt will still have to comply with conditions and will be subject to supervision. But when parole boards get it wrong, the consequences can be fatal.
Link: It seems that Parole Boards around the country have allowed killers and paedophiles to slip though the bars and released them back into the community. The results have been tragic.

V/O: In February this year, a convicted murderer who was out on parole, allegedly killed his four children in Limpopo. He’d previously been jailed for murdering his neighbour’s child, but was released on parole.

Also in February, 8 year-old Reagan Gertse was raped and murdered in Tulbagh allegedly by a family member. The community protested outside the bail hearing of the suspect who was previously convicted of raping a 5-year old boy, but released on parole.

Judge: There is a high rate of recidivism in this country. Those crimes are of a particular serious nature, and that requires a high degree of careful consideration before they can possibly be released. People who have committed very serious offenses, or have committed multiple rapes and murders, that sort of offender one could never release.

Luke: The idea that men who are on parole rape and kill I find to be – of the travesties of justice we have in the world – of the greatest. I mean it just talks to the entire system being completely broken in terms of the protection and safety of children.
